title: From v1.22, with subnet discovery on, ENI creation stops when ec2:DescribeSubnets is denied

detection.reason: the CNI role's IAM policy is AWS-side; ENABLE_SUBNET_DISCOVERY's VALUE is not collected

quote: Enhanced subnet discovery - allow customers to exclude specific subnets from pod allocation by tagging with `kubernetes.io/role/cni=0`
remediation: v1.22 checks, before creating a secondary ENI, whether the subnet is excluded by a kubernetes.io/role/cni=0 tag (e97bfe7e, IsSubnetExcluded), which calls ec2:DescribeSubnets again. With ENABLE_SUBNET_DISCOVERY on (the default) a failed call aborts the attempt ("Quit ENI creation attempt"), so a node whose CNI role lacks ec2:DescribeSubnets stops growing ENIs and new pods wait for IPs once the warm pool drains (v1.23.2's fail-open fix covers ipamd's setup path only). Grant ec2:DescribeSubnets (it is in AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy's documented set since v1.18.4) or set ENABLE_SUBNET_DISCOVERY=false before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get ds aws-node -o json | jq -r '"ENABLE_SUBNET_DISCOVERY=" + ([.spec.template.spec.containers[] | .env[]? | select(.name == "ENABLE_SUBNET_DISCOVERY") | .value][0] // "(unset = true)")'  # true/unset = the CNI role (IRSA role of the aws-node service account, else the node role) must allow ec2:DescribeSubnets
